title: How to Bake Sourdough Potato Rolls on a Sheet Pan
meta_description: Learn how to bake fluffy sourdough potato rolls on a sheet pan using a silicone baking mat for perfect non‑stick results and zero‑scrub cleanup.
html:
If you’ve ever struggled to keep rolls from sticking or ending up with a soggy bottom, a silicone baking mat is the game‑changer you need. This guide shows you step‑by‑step how to bake sourdough potato rolls on a sheet pan, why the sourdough potato rolls silicone mat is essential, and how to get a golden crust every time.

Why Use a Silicone Baking Mat for Sourdough Potato Rolls

A silicone baking mat provides three key benefits that plain parchment or bare metal can’t match. First, the non‑stick surface lets the rolls release cleanly, preserving their delicate crumb. Second, the mat distributes heat evenly, preventing hot spots that can over‑brown the bottoms. Third, because the mat is reusable, you eliminate the waste and cost of parchment while enjoying a cleanup that’s literally a wipe‑off.

Ingredients and Tools

Gather these items before you start. Having everything measured and ready will keep the dough from over‑working.

  • 1 cup active sourdough starter (100% hydration)
  • 1 ½ cups warm water (about 95°F)
  • 2 ¼ teaspoons instant yeast
  • 3 ½ cups bread flour
  • ½ cup mashed potatoes (cooled)
  • 2 teaspoons salt
  • 2 tablespoons unsalted butter, melted
  • Silicone Baking Mat (the non‑stick, reusable mat that replaces parchment)
  • 2‑quart sheet pan
  • Bench scraper, kitchen scale, and a clean kitchen towel

Step‑by‑Step: Mixing and Fermenting the Dough

1. Activate the starter. In a large bowl, combine the starter, warm water, and instant yeast. Stir for 30 seconds to dissolve the yeast; the mixture will look slightly foamy.

2. Incorporate the dry ingredients. Add the bread flour, mashed potatoes, and salt to the bowl. Using a dough hook or your hands, mix until the dough pulls away from the sides. It should be shaggy but cohesive.

3. Knead. Transfer the dough to a lightly floured surface and knead for about 8‑10 minutes, or until it becomes smooth and elastic. The potatoes keep the crumb tender while the sourdough adds flavor.

4. First rise. Lightly oil the bowl, place the dough inside, and cover with a damp towel. Let it rise at room temperature (around 70°F) for 2‑3 hours, or until doubled in size.

5. Cold retard. For best flavor, cover the dough tightly and place it in the refrigerator for an additional 12‑18 hours. This slow fermentation deepens the sourdough tang.

Shaping and Baking on a Sheet Pan

When the dough is ready, it’s time to shape the rolls and use your silicone mat.

1. Pre‑heat the oven. Set the oven to 425°F and let it fully heat for at least 20 minutes. A hot oven gives the rolls a quick rise and a crisp crust.

2. Prepare the pan. Lay the silicone baking mat on a 2‑quart sheet pan. No spray or parchment is needed—the mat’s non‑stick surface does the work.

3. Shape the rolls. Turn the dough out onto a lightly floured board. Divide it into 12 equal pieces (about 1.5 ounces each). Shape each piece into a smooth ball, then place them on the mat, spacing them about 2 inches apart. The mat prevents them from spreading into each other.

4. Second rise. Cover the rolls loosely with a clean kitchen towel and let them proof for 30‑45 minutes, until they look puffy but haven’t doubled.

5. Bake. Slide the pan onto the middle rack. Bake for 15‑18 minutes, or until the tops are deep golden and the bottoms feel firm to the touch. The silicone mat conducts heat evenly, so you’ll get a uniform crust without a burnt bottom.

6. Cool. Remove the pan from the oven and let the rolls rest on the mat for 5 minutes before transferring them to a wire rack. This short cooling period lets steam escape, keeping the crust crisp.

Tips for Perfect Rolls Every Time

• Don’t over‑mix the potato. Over‑working the mashed potatoes can make the dough gummy. Add them just until incorporated.

• Use a kitchen scale. Weighing flour and potatoes gives consistent results, especially when humidity changes.

• Watch the oven temperature. If your rolls brown too quickly, rotate the pan halfway through baking.

• Reuse the silicone mat. After baking, let the mat cool, then wipe it with a damp cloth. No scrubbing needed—no harsh chemicals, no parchment waste.

Storing and Reheating

Once cooled, store the rolls in an airtight container at room temperature for up to three days. For a quick reheating, place them on the silicone mat in a 350°F oven for 5‑7 minutes; the mat keeps the bottoms from getting soggy while reviving the crust.

FAQ

Can I use a regular silicone baking mat for gluten‑free rolls?

Yes. The mat’s non‑stick surface works with any dough, but gluten‑free batters may spread more. Lightly dust the mat with flour if needed.

Do I need to grease the silicone mat before baking?

No. The silicone baking mat is designed to be completely non‑stick without any oil or spray.

How do I clean the mat after baking a sticky dough?

Allow the mat to cool, then wipe it with a warm, damp cloth. For stubborn residue, a gentle dish soap rinse is fine; avoid abrasive pads.
